requirement_catalog.statement: alpha_m and beta_n are supported on single factor-two intervals.
requirement_catalog.evidence: CP-0003 gives a rigorous fine multiplicative cell construction for G9: beta is supported in [P,rho P] and alpha in [UV,rho^2 UV], both contained in factor-two intervals when rho^3<=4. The G11/G12 rough-residual cells are not yet compiled.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Construct the corresponding G11/G12 alpha cells with the Buchstab-counted rough residual.

requirement_catalog.statement: Both sequences obey one fixed divisor-function order bound.
requirement_catalog.evidence: For every G9 cell beta<=1 and alpha_m counts ordered prime pairs p2*p3=m, hence alpha_m<=tau_2(m). The fixed-order bound for the G11/G12 rough-residual alpha sequence remains open.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Prove a uniform fixed-order divisor bound for the G11/G12 complementary rough-factor sequence.

requirement_catalog.condition: beta_n is the characteristic function of primes in one frozen p1 cell, with (n,N_global)=1.
requirement_catalog.evidence: Siegel-Walfisz on the frozen interval gives the residue-class main term. Removing primes dividing d or N_global is absorbed by the tau_h(d) error; the h=1 case is exact.
requirement_catalog.cannot_imply: The switched decomposition must still establish that beta is p1 in each call.

requirement_catalog.statement: The prime-supported beta_n satisfies the small-prime-factor exclusion.
requirement_catalog.condition: orientation O1 and sufficiently large p1 cells.
requirement_catalog.evidence: A sufficiently large prime has no proper prime factor below exp((log log n)^2).
requirement_catalog.cannot_imply: Does not establish the orientation or the remaining call data.

requirement_catalog.statement: The local scale is frozen for every cell.
requirement_catalog.evidence: For every G9 interior cell, set beta support P, alpha support M=UV, Li-Liu scale X=MP and primary-source scale x=4MP. Product support is at most rho^3 MP<=x. G11/G12 cells remain open.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Freeze the G11/G12 cell scales after reconstructing their alpha sequences.

requirement_catalog.statement: nu is computed from the primary-source local scale.
requirement_catalog.evidence: For G9 interior cells CP-0003 uses nu=log(P)/log(x) with x=4MP, matching Fouvry's normalization rather than silently using log(P)/log(MP).
requirement_catalog.next_action: Apply the same normalization to G11/G12 after their cell construction.

requirement_catalog.statement: The low-p1 family can be split so epsilon_lemma<=nu<=1/10 exactly.
requirement_catalog.evidence: Use rho^3<=4 and t=p1*m>=epsilon0*N_global. Then x=4MP>=epsilon0*N_global. Restrict the enhanced-level cells to p1<=c_epsilon*N_global^(1/10), c_epsilon=epsilon0^(1/10); hence P^10<=epsilon0*N_global<=x and nu<=1/10. The fixed-ratio top slice has reciprocal-prime mass O_epsilon(1/log N_global) and can be sent to the coefficient-8 method with O_epsilon(N_global/log^3 N_global) loss. The lower endpoint 4/53 is separated from epsilon_lemma for large N_global.
requirement_catalog.cannot_imply: The top-slice transition loss must be included in the global signed error ledger.

requirement_catalog.statement: lambda is order-1 well-factorable at the asserted cell level.
requirement_catalog.evidence: Lemma 2.5 produces finitely many order-1 well-factorable lambda_l^+ at its chosen level; Lemma 3.5 may be applied separately to each l. The exact cellwise identification and the dependence of L=exp(8 eta^-3) remain to be bound.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Bind each cell's Q to the exact Lemma 2.5 remainder weight and record the L dependence.

requirement_catalog.statement: The linear-sieve level matches the primary-source mean-value level.
requirement_catalog.evidence: With x=4MP and nu=log P/log x the primary level is x^(5(1-nu)/9-delta). The factor-four difference from Li-Liu's X=MP is harmless after retuning the arbitrary exponent loss, but the actual sieve Q must be frozen cell by cell.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Compare the generated Lemma 2.5 level with x^(5(1-nu)/9-delta) for every interior cell.

requirement_catalog.statement: The global residue N_global lies in a fixed-multiple uniformity range of the primary theorem for every admissible product cell.
requirement_catalog.evidence: Fouvry uses x=4MP and states |a|<=x. His proof remarks that |a| enters only through integration by parts and tau(a), so for fixed C the same proof is uniform for |a|<=C x. In an admissible cell t=p1*m>=epsilon0*N_global and t<=rho^3 MP<=x, hence N_global<=x/epsilon0. Apply the fixed-multiple extension with C=epsilon0^-1; its constant is allowed to depend on the paper's fixed epsilon0.
requirement_catalog.verification_required: A fresh verifier must inspect the complete Fouvry proof of the C-dependent extension.
requirement_catalog.cannot_imply: Does not close the cell decomposition, Q matching or error summation.

requirement_catalog.statement: The theorem error is uniform over compiled cells and fixed residue multiplier.
requirement_catalog.evidence: The fixed-multiple residue extension changes only the epsilon0-dependent implied constant. Interior G9 cells use one fixed mesh exponent J and fixed sequence order, so their theorem constants are uniform. Boundary-cell and Lemma 2.5 L-dependence remain open.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Add boundary and L dependencies to the sibling common-error ledger.

requirement_catalog.statement: All cell errors sum within a selectable logarithmic saving.
requirement_catalog.evidence: A rho=exp((log N)^(-J)) grid has polylogarithmically many G9 interior cells. Lemma 3.5 allows arbitrary A, so choosing A beyond the grid exponent absorbs all interior theorem errors. Product-boundary cells crossing epsilon0*N_global or N_global still need a signed upper-cover or smooth hyperbolic partition.
requirement_catalog.next_action: Prove the product-boundary contribution or replace the hard cutoff by a source-backed smooth/Mellin partition.

requirement_catalog.statement: The distribution level yields the displayed 36/5 and 8 coefficients.
requirement_catalog.condition: The cellwise x, nu and Q have been validly instantiated.
requirement_catalog.evidence: Upper-bound monotonicity lowers the sifting threshold to Q^(1/2), where s=2. The normalizer is 4/theta(nu); theta(nu)=5(1-nu)/9 gives 36/[5(1-nu)] and value 8 at nu=1/10.
requirement_catalog.cannot_imply: The exact coefficient bridge does not establish the remaining theorem hypotheses.

g9_box_compiler.alpha_cell: alpha_UV(m)=# {(p2,p3): U<=p2<rho U, V<=p3<rho V, p2<=p3, p2*p3=m, (m,N_global)=1}

g9_box_compiler.redundant_constraint: p2<=(N_global/p1)^(1/2) follows from p3>=p2 and p1*p2*p3<=N_global
g9_box_compiler.interior_error_sum: absorbed by choosing the arbitrary A larger than the mesh exponent

findings.statement: Lemma 3.5 has materially asymmetric assumptions on beta_n.
findings.cannot_imply: Does not show that no valid orientation exists.

findings.statement: Taking beta_n to be the smallest prime p1 is the structurally preferred orientation.
findings.cannot_imply: The exact switched convolution and local scales still require reconstruction.

findings.statement: For theta(nu)=5(1-nu)/9, 4/theta(nu)=36/[5(1-nu)] and the value at nu=1/10 is 8.
findings.cannot_imply: Coefficient matching does not verify a theorem call.

findings.statement: A frozen prime p1 block satisfies condition (3.2) by Siegel-Walfisz, including exclusions for d and N_global.
findings.cannot_imply: Requires the call decomposition to put p1 in beta.

findings.statement: For G9 the sifted residual is prime outside explicitly bounded squareful-p1 and divisor-of-N_global branches.
findings.cannot_imply: The resulting multiset still needs a rigorous cell decomposition.

findings.statement: The z<=Q^(1/2) restriction is reconciled by upper-bound monotonicity, producing 4/theta(nu).
findings.cannot_imply: Does not validate Q or nu in a concrete cell.

findings.statement: G11/G12 contain a Buchstab-counted rough residual and cannot be modeled as one additional prime.
findings.cannot_imply: The corrected alpha sequence has not yet been bounded by a fixed tau_k.

findings.statement: Fouvry's Corollary 2(i) uses x=4MN and nu=log N/log x; Li-Liu's Lemma 3.5 writes X=MN.
findings.cannot_imply: The fixed-factor normalization difference alone does not invalidate the application.

findings.statement: For each fixed C>=1, Fouvry Corollary 2(i) extends uniformly from |a|<=x to |a|<=C x with a C-dependent implied constant.
proof_spine: Fouvry states that the magnitude of a enters only in integration by parts and through tau(a).
The derivative bounds acquire only a fixed C factor when |a|<=C x.
tau(a)<<_delta |a|^delta<=C^delta x^delta, which is absorbed by the arbitrary internal power/log slack.
findings.cannot_imply: This solver proof candidate needs an independent check of every occurrence of a in the primary proof.

findings.statement: The enhanced-level family can be trimmed to p1<=epsilon0^(1/10) N_global^(1/10), giving nu<=1/10 exactly; the constant-ratio top slice costs O_epsilon(N_global/log^3 N_global) under the coefficient-8 treatment.
findings.cannot_imply: The transition term is not yet integrated into the global signed error ledger.

findings.statement: A fine multiplicative grid gives valid G9 interior alpha/beta cells with beta prime-supported, alpha<=tau_2, primary scale x=4MP and polylogarithmically summable theorem errors.
findings.cannot_imply: Cells crossing the two product cutoffs still require a rigorous signed treatment.

findings.statement: After CP-0003 the earliest G9 obstruction is no longer the residue size or nu endpoint; it is the exact treatment of product-boundary cells together with cellwise Q/weight binding.
findings.cannot_imply: The complete G9 call is not yet PASS.

The remaining G9 work is to treat cells crossing the product cutoffs without losing the signed remainder and to bind each cell to the actual well-factorable Q.
